explanation: In C++, operator overloading allows developers to define or customize the behavior of operators (such as <, +, ==) for user-defined types, enabling intuitive syntax and integration with standard algorithms. Specifically, overloading comparison operators like operator< facilitates custom ordering logic, which is essential for containers like std::set or std::map. When overloading operators involving smart pointers such as std::unique_ptr, it ensures that comparisons are meaningful and consistent with the semantics of the managed objects. Modern C++ allows overloading operators as free functions, often as templates, to extend their applicability and enable comparisons between different types, such as between nullptr_t and smart pointers.
syntax:
template <typename T, typename D>
bool operator<(std::nullptr_t, const std::unique_ptr<T, D>& y);
